issue.title: URL dedupe keys treat %40 and @ in a path as different sources

task_type_fields.impact:
URL dedupe (`bob ref create`, ingest, `bob capture` routing) and `bob ref find` treat one
article as two sources when its URL arrives with `%40` instead of `@`, so the article can
be captured twice and library lookup misses the twin. It also weakens the duplicate-URL
check planned for multi-URL `bob ref create` collections
(research:202610/ref_create_multi_url_collections/ref_create_multi_url_collections__final.md §6).
task_type_fields.repro:
Repro on bob-cli `ba71710` with the live vault:

1. `bob ref find 'https://medium.com/@edominguez.se/so-i-switched-to-neovim-in-2025-163b85aa0935'`
   reports only `ref/zorg/nvim_ref/nvim_from_scratch_2025.md`.
2. `bob ref list -R all -A -o external -f json` shows a second note for the same article,
   `i_switched_to_nvim`, whose identity key is
   `https://medium.com/%40edominguez.se/so-i-switched-to-neovim-in-2025-163b85aa0935`,
   while `nvim_from_scratch_2025` keys on `https://medium.com/@edominguez.se/...`.
   Neither row carries `duplicate_identity` or `superseded_by`.

Root cause: `dedupe_key_for` (`src/native/highlights_ref/clip_url.rs:79`) appends
`url.path()` verbatim. The `url` crate preserves percent-escapes, so `%40` and `@` (and,
by the same path, other escaped characters that are legal literally in a path segment, or
lowercase vs uppercase hex escapes) produce different dedupe keys. Medium share links
commonly arrive in both spellings.

Suggested fix: percent-normalize the path when building the key (decode escapes of
characters that are valid literally in a path segment, such as RFC 3986 unreserved
characters and `@`, and uppercase the remaining hex escapes), then add a
`dedupe_key_normalizes_spellings`-style unit test for `%40` vs `@`. Check how the same key
feeds `ref_library` identity and supersession, so that existing twin notes start to
report `duplicate_identity` or supersession as expected.

issue.creation_reason: Found while evaluating multi-URL naming over the live reference library: two notes for the same Medium article have different identity keys, so ref find and capture dedupe miss the twin.

payload.entry: Fixed by batch 7: phase .1 commit f2524e80 normalizes path escapes in the shared dedupe key (unreserved escapes decode, retained escapes uppercase, encoded / ? # % never merge, no recursive decode); the batch-7 lander narrowed the reserved @ rule (landing commit for bob-cli-an.6.6.6.5.6.5) so %40 aliases @ only for the leading author sigil of the first path segment on exact medium.com (after www.), keeping example.com/a%40b distinct from /a@b and lookalike hosts, Medium subdomains, and non-author %40 escaped. The reported medium.com/@edominguez.se vs %40edominguez.se pair shares one key; ref find returns both twins with duplicate_identity (CLI find_medium_twins_are_one_identity), create dedupe refuses the twin, collection overlap detects it, and a reserved non-Medium %40 path is not refused. Stored source_url unchanged; contract documented in docs/highlights-clip.md. Verified: new regressions fail with the old blanket @ decode and pass now; focused lib dedupe_key/reserved_at_sign/twin tests 10/10; just check exit 0 (3411 lib, 2052 CLI).
